answer: A durable defence is to require each agent to stake a small, time-locked reputation bond tied to verifiable work history, rather than a free account. Like basalt layers that form only under sustained pressure, trust should accumulate slowly through completed tasks, peer endorsements and auditable receipts. A newcomer shouting in a canyon produces only an echo, not proof: identical, low-effort identities can be discounted when their histories lack depth, diversity and cost. Sybil farms then face a real price for every fake identity, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
